title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
subtitle: A decade of P&L cycles, depreciation drag, other-income spikes, rising project debt, and working-capital discipline

web_blocks.html: Over the ten-year span from FY2015 through FY2026 (noting FY2020–FY2021 omissions in the standard consolidated snapshot), ZF Steering Gear's consolidated top line expanded from ₹351 crore to ₹571 crore. Reached ₹645 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026 [1]. Yet profit growth did not track revenue growth. Operating profit in FY2026 (₹75 crore) still sat below the ₹82–84 crore achieved in FY2017–FY2018. Meanwhile, net profit fell from ₹43–44 crore in FY2018–FY2019 to ₹12–13 crore in FY2025–FY2026 [1]. Rising depreciation (from ₹27 crore to ₹47 crore), higher interest costs (₹1 crore to ₹8 crore). An elevated 58% effective tax rate in FY2026 absorbed the incremental operating profit [1].

web_blocks.caption: ZFSTEERING: Multi-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (₹ Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sales reached record highs in FY2026 (₹571 Cr) and TTM Sep 2026 (₹645 Cr), but higher depreciation (₹47 Cr) and finance costs (₹8 Cr) kept FY2026 net profit at ₹12 Cr versus ₹44 Cr in FY2024.

web_blocks.html: A critical forensic detail in the P&L is the volatility of Other Income. In FY2024, Other Income surged to ₹34 crore—accounting for 65% of the ₹52 crore Profit Before Tax—before normalizing to ₹21 crore in FY2025 and ₹9 crore in FY2026 [1]. In Q1 FY2027 (June 2026), Other Income spiked again to ₹15 crore out of ₹16 crore PBT [1]. Owners must therefore strip out treasury gains and evaluate core Operating Profit (₹75 crore in FY2026; ₹26 crore in Q2 FY27 alone) rather than headline PAT [1].

web_blocks.caption: ZFSTEERING: Consolidated Balance Sheet Trajectory (₹ Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Total assets more than doubled from ₹317 Cr (Mar 2015) to ₹760 Cr (Sep 2026), funded by retained earnings (₹496 Cr reserves) and a steady rise in borrowings to ₹165 Cr.

web_blocks.html: Balance-sheet forensics show an asset-heavy build-out phase. Fixed assets plus Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) rose from ₹161 crore in March 2022 to ₹298 crore in March 2026 and ₹330 crore by September 2026, with CWIP alone hitting ₹103 crore [1]. To fund this expansion without diluting equity (Share Capital remained fixed at ₹9 crore), management drew down liquid investments from ₹156 crore in March 2025 to ₹135–136 crore and increased consolidated borrowings from ₹34 crore in March 2022 to ₹165 crore in September 2026 [1]. Even after that increase, net debt remains modest (roughly ₹29 crore net of the ₹136 crore investment book, or ~0.33x gross debt-to-equity). This explains why ICRA reaffirmed its [ICRA]A+ (Stable) parent rating [1][8].

web_blocks.caption: ZFSTEERING: Consolidated Cash Flow & Free Cash Flow Profile (₹ Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating cash flow conversion is strong (₹98 Cr CFO in FY2026, 145% of EBITDA), but heavy capex kept Free Cash Flow negative across FY2024 (-₹55 Cr), FY2025 (-₹19 Cr), and FY2026 (-₹11 Cr).

web_blocks.html: Cash-flow quality at the operating level is one of ZF Steering Gear's genuine strengths. Pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA conversion averaged 96%–152% in strong years and reached 145% in FY2026 as ₹98 crore of cash arrived from operations [1]. The entire cash drain occurs in Cash from Investing Activity (-₹52 crore in FY2024, -₹64 crore in FY2025, and -₹89 crore in FY2026), producing three consecutive years of negative Free Cash Flow [1].

web_blocks.caption: ZFSTEERING: Working Capital Efficiency & Return Ratios
web_blocks.takeaway: Working capital discipline improved dramatically (21 days in FY2026 vs. 103 in FY2022), yet ROCE compressed to 6% in FY2025–FY2026 from 15%–18% in FY2016–FY2018.

web_blocks.html: The efficiency ratios crystallize the price-blind verdict on business quality. Working capital management is best-in-class for a Tier-1 auto ancillary: debtor days dropped from 105 in FY2022 to 64 in FY2026, inventory days fell from 110 to 73. Net working capital days compressed to 21 [1]. Yet consolidated ROCE sits at 6.48% and ROE at 3.29%, roughly half of a typical 11%–12% Indian corporate cost of capital [1]. Until the ₹103 crore CWIP commissions and DriveSys lifts consolidated EBIT, ZF Steering Gear remains a cyclical industrial compounder-in-waiting rather than a high-ROCE franchise.

A final balance-sheet check confirms that ZF Steering Gear has avoided equity dilution over the past decade, keeping equity share capital steady at ~₹9.07 Cr while funding expansion via internal accruals and moderate debt (0.33x debt-to-equity) [8, 23]. Avoiding dilutive equity raises protects per-share compounding power if DriveSys and core steering deliver mid-teens operating margins.

Stress-testing interest coverage shows that TTM operating profit (₹84 Cr) comfortably covers annualised interest expense (~₹12–₹15 Cr at current ₹165 Cr gross debt), keeping solvency risk low (0.33x debt-to-equity) [8, 23]. Nonetheless, quarterly interest costs have risen from near zero in FY24 to ₹2–₹5 Cr per quarter. This makes debt paydown essential if M&HCV demand softens [8].
Tax-rate normalization around ~25% and steady working-capital turns near 21 days provide a clean bridge from operating profit to operating cash flow once capex intensity tapers [8].
Zero share dilution over ten years protects per-share upside if margins hold. Still, ₹165 Cr of borrowings and ₹47 Cr of annual depreciation raise the bar for net profit.

epigraph.quote: Balance sheets never lie about strategy: when CWIP hits ₹103 crore and ROCE sits at 6 percent, the company is asking owners to wait for tomorrow's utilization.
epigraph.author: Pass 1 Forensic Principle

book_paragraphs: When you lay out ten years of ZF Steering Gear's financial statements side by side, one pattern stands out immediately: revenue has grown to record highs, but net profit has not followed it up. Consolidated sales climbed from ₹351 crore in FY2015 to ₹571 crore in FY2026, and ₹645 crore over the trailing twelve months ended September 2026. Yet net profit in FY2026 was just ₹12 crore—less than a third of the ₹43 crore earned back in FY2018. Why? Because depreciation jumped from ₹27 crore to ₹47 crore as the new plants came online, interest rose to ₹8 crore, and the effective tax rate hit 58%.

You also have to watch Other Income carefully so you do not mistake treasury gains for factory profits. In FY2024, Other Income contributed ₹34 crore out of ₹52 crore in pre-tax profit, making the year look far stronger than core operations justified. The same thing happened in the June 2026 quarter, when ₹15 crore of Other Income accounted for almost all of the ₹16 crore pre-tax profit. Always look at Operating Profit—₹75 crore in FY2026 and ₹26 crore in the September 2026 quarter—to judge the real health of the plants.

On the balance sheet, total assets have more than doubled over the decade to ₹760 crore by September 2026. Fixed assets and Capital Work-in-Progress now stand at ₹330 crore, with CWIP alone at ₹103 crore. To pay for those plants without issuing new shares, the company trimmed its investment portfolio to ₹136 crore and raised borrowings from ₹34 crore in 2022 to ₹165 crore by September 2026. Even with that debt, the balance sheet remains conservative—gross debt is roughly a third of net worth, and ICRA maintains an [ICRA]A+ Stable rating on the parent.

The cash-flow statement confirms that the factories convert earnings into cash cleanly: operating cash flow hit ₹98 crore in FY2026, or 145% of operating profit before tax, aided by working capital shrinking from 103 days in FY2022 to 21 days in FY2026. The reason free cash flow stayed negative for three straight years—minus ₹55 crore in FY2024, minus ₹19 crore in FY2025, and minus ₹11 crore in FY2026—is purely heavy capital spending. With ROCE sitting at 6.48% and ROE at 3.29%, the business is clearly earning below its cost of capital right now. That is why we classify ZF Steering Gear as a cyclical conditional business: the core steering duopoly and working capital are sound, but owner returns depend entirely on turning ₹330 crore of plant assets into double-digit ROCE.
Always test headline earnings against depreciation, interest, and working-capital cash flow before committing equity capital to any cyclical manufacturer.

book_callouts.title: Ten-Year Forensic Checkpoints
book_callouts.quote: Strong operating cash conversion (145% CFO/EBITDA in FY26) is currently offset by three years of negative free cash flow and sub-7% ROCE.
bullets: Other Income inflated FY24 PBT (₹34 Cr of ₹52 Cr) and Q1 FY27 PBT (₹15 Cr of ₹16 Cr).
Borrowings rose from ₹34 Cr (Mar 2022) to ₹165 Cr (Sep 2026), still ~0.33x equity.
Working capital days fell to 21, but ROCE (6.48%) trails cost of capital.

book_subsections.title: Separating Operating Cash Flow from Other Income Optics
paragraphs: Chapter 6 is where we put the ten-year financial statements under a forensic microscope. Look closely at two lines in the quarterly and annual profit-and-loss tables: Other Income and Interest Expense [8].

In trailing twelve-month results through September 2026, Other Income contributed ₹23 Cr—including a ₹15 Cr spike in Q1 FY27 alone [8]. At the same time, quarterly interest expense crept up from negligible levels in FY24 to ₹2–₹5 Cr per quarter as consolidated borrowings expanded from ₹34 Cr in March 2022 to ₹165 Cr by September 2026 [8].

For an analyst, that means you must judge ZF Steering Gear on its pre-other-income operating profit (EBITDA of ₹84 Cr over the TTM period, or ~13 percent margin) rather than net profit alone [8]. Encouragingly, Q2 FY27 operating profit hit ₹26 Cr at a 14 percent margin on ₹184 Cr of sales, showing real core operating leverage [8].

book_subsections.title: The Balance Sheet Question: When Does CWIP Become Cash?
paragraphs: Every rupee of the ₹103 Cr Capital Work-in-Progress sitting on the September 2026 balance sheet represents capital already spent that is not yet earning its keep [8]. That single line item explains why consolidated ROCE sits at 6.48 percent and ROE at 3.29 percent despite healthy cash conversion from operations [8].

Notice that operating cash flow in FY26 was ₹98 Cr—a strong number—but ₹109 Cr of capex consumed all of it [8]. Once the Supa and Pune expansion wave concludes, if maintenance capex settles near ₹25–₹35 Cr a year while operating cash flow holds above ₹90 Cr, the business can quickly generate ₹55–₹65 Cr of annual free cash flow and retire debt.

book_subsections.title: Why Zero Share Dilution Protects Upside
paragraphs: One of the quietest virtues in ZF Steering Gear's ten-year financial history is the absence of equity dilution. With only 90.73 lakh shares outstanding, management did not flood the market with preferential allotments or QIPs to fund the Supa aluminium plant.

Instead, they leaned on internal cash flow and ₹165 Cr of borrowings [8]. That keeps leverage moderate at 0.33 times equity and means that if consolidated net profit scales from ₹32 Cr toward ₹54–₹72 Cr over the next two years, every rupee of earnings growth flows straight to existing shareholders on a per-share basis.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Resilience Under a Slowdown Scenario
paragraphs: Before you ever buy a cyclical industrial stock, you must ask: what happens if the economy hits an air pocket tomorrow? With ₹165 Cr of consolidated borrowings against roughly ₹505 Cr of net worth (book value ₹557 per share across 90.73 lakh shares), debt-to-equity is a conservative 0.33 times [8, 23].

Trailing operating profit of ₹84 Cr covers annual interest charges roughly six times over [8]. That means ZF Steering Gear is nowhere near financial distress even if truck sales dip for a couple of quarters.
Still, rising interest expense eats directly into net profit when margins compress. Paying down debt with free cash flow over FY27 and FY28 is the fastest way to de-risk the equity story.

book_subsections.title: Why Clean Accounting Makes Forensic Work Easier
paragraphs: One comforting feature of ZF Steering Gear's ten-year accounts is that cash flow from operations tracks operating profit closely once working capital is adjusted. In FY26, ₹98 Cr of operating cash flow on ₹63 Cr of operating profit confirms there are no hidden receivable write-offs.
The sole drag on free cash flow has been deliberate factory investment—something that can turn off quickly once the Supa expansion is complete.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Ten-Year Cash Flow Story
paragraphs: Stepping back across a full decade of financial statements, the overarching lesson is clear: ZF Steering Gear has never suffered from accounting gimmicks or reckless equity dilution, but it has struggled to earn high returns on incremental capital during heavy investment phases [8].
As the current capex cycle winds down, the company's ability to convert ₹98 Cr of annual operating cash flow into genuine, distributable free cash flow will decide its next valuation regime [8].

book_subsections.title: The Link Between Asset Turns and Return on Capital
paragraphs: Return on capital employed is simply operating profit margin multiplied by capital turnover. A business can improve ROCE either by raising margins or by generating more sales from every rupee of plant and equipment.

At ZF Steering Gear, margins have already recovered into the 13 to 14 percent range in recent quarters, yet consolidated ROCE remains stuck at 6.48 percent because ₹103 Cr of capital work-in-progress is not yet producing full revenue [8]. That math explains why CWIP conversion is the single most important balance-sheet milestone ahead.

book_subsections.title: Why Depreciation and Debt Service Set the Hurdle
paragraphs: A clean share count of 90.73 lakh shares ensures that any future earnings recovery accrues directly to existing owners without dilution. At the same time, ₹165 Cr of consolidated debt and ₹47 Cr of annual depreciation create a substantial fixed charge ahead of net profit.
Retiring debt out of operating cash flow over FY27 and FY28 is therefore essential to lift net margins and restore return on equity toward double digits.
